NDT training in Ogden, UT: how it works for Ogden employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Ogden technicians and employers is self-paced online theory, with Level III questions answered by an ASNT NDT Level III, followed by hands-on practice in person at the employer's own facility. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Ogden. The training is based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and the employer certifies. We reply within one business day.

Ogden is one of the clearest aerospace and defence markets in the Mountain West. Aircraft depot maintenance at Hill Air Force Base, engine manufacturing, rocket motor work and a long list of machine shops and composite fabricators create a steady need for NDT technicians who can follow a precise procedure and keep exact records.

That shapes what a good training plan looks like. In aerospace, the method is only half the job; the other half is traceability. An examiner may have to show which procedure was used, which equipment was calibrated, and which certification covered the technician on the day. A course that teaches documentation habits alongside technique is more useful here than one that only covers the physics.

Request a Ogden training quote, and tell us the methods, levels and head-count you have in mind. In Ogden, anyone planning ahead can also read the NDT training FAQ, the Atlantis training overview and the USA training page.

How to get NDT certified in Ogden: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Certification in Utah follows the same pattern as elsewhere in the United States. In Ogden, under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies its own technicians, and the standard is a set of recommended practices that each employer turns into a written practice of its own. Here is the sequence in order.

  1. Find or have an employer with a written practice. A technician in Ogden is certified by the company that employs them, so the first step is a sponsor whose written practice covers the method and level you want. In Ogden, the practice sets the hours, the examinations and the recertification interval.
  2. In Ogden, complete the formal training. Take the classroom hours the written practice requires. The training-requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours for each method, and your Ogden employer may set higher figures.
  3. Log supervised experience. Document the hours a Ogden technician spends performing the method under a certified Level II or III. Experience is usually the slowest part for a new Ogden technician, so start the log from the first day on a job.
  4. In Ogden, pass the general examination on principles, equipment and terminology for the method.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the procedures, equipment and acceptance standards your Ogden employer really uses.
  6. In Ogden, pass the practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner working under one.
  7. In Ogden, pass the vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation at the intervals the written practice sets. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows what to expect.
  8. Receive certification signed by your Ogden employer.
  9. In Ogden, recertify at the interval the written practice sets, which SNT-TC-1A recommends should not exceed five years, by examination or documented performance as permitted.

In Ogden, ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, and ASNT NDT Level III examinations) is the alternative if you want a credential that stays with you rather than with an employer. Atlantis prepares candidates for that route too. See ASNT certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Ogden technicians

In Ogden, each course follows the body of knowledge in SNT-TC-1A for its method. In Ogden, level 1 courses cover the fundamentals and working under supervision, Level 2 courses cover setting up, calibrating, performing and evaluating examinations to a procedure, and Level 3 preparation covers the basic and method examinations for those who will write procedures and examine others.

Method What the course covers Where it is used around Ogden
UT Sound physics, calibration, thickness and bond checks, angle-beam examination, reporting Metal and composite component checks, structural thickness, weld examination in fabrication
RT In Ogden, exposure technique, image quality, film and digital interpretation, radiation safety basics Castings, welds and assemblies where customer specifications call for radiography
MT Magnetising methods, field direction, particle application, indication evaluation Steel forgings, landing gear-type components and ground support equipment
PT Process control, dwell times, cleaning, indication interpretation Surface cracks in non-ferrous parts, machined components, castings
VT Acuity and lighting, discontinuities, measuring tools, reporting First-line examination on fabricated assemblies, welds and fastener and surface condition checks
PAUT In Ogden, focal laws, encoded scanning, data analysis, sizing (UT Level II first) Welds and components where the customer specification permits phased array
TOFD Diffraction technique, setup, flaw sizing (UT Level II first) Heavy-section welds on pressure equipment and industrial fabrications

In Ogden, PAUT and TOFD are advanced ultrasonic techniques and are generally taken after UT Level II. In Ogden, whether they can be used on a given job depends on the customer's specification and the employer's written practice.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Ogden

In an aerospace-heavy market such as Ogden, ultrasonic testing is applied in ways that differ from a refinery. Components are smaller and more precisely machined, material may be steel, aluminium, titanium or composite, and procedures are written for one part and one set-up rather than for a general weld. A Level I UT course teaches the physics, equipment set-up and calibration, while Level II adds more demanding evaluation and reporting against the acceptance criteria in the procedure.

Because aerospace procedures are specific, a technician is expected to follow the procedure exactly, not interpret it loosely. Practising set-ups repeatedly is the way to build that habit, and the Practical NDT simulator is a useful rehearsal tool between hands-on sessions. The ultrasonic testing training page lists the course content, and the UT Level 2 practice questions help with the general examination.

Where NDT technicians work around Ogden

Hill Air Force Base and its supplier network. Hill AFB is home to the Ogden Air Logistics Complex, a major depot for fighter aircraft maintenance and weapons systems support, and it is one of the largest employers in northern Utah. Depot work follows military technical orders, and contractors supporting it operate under their own quality programmes. SNT-TC-1A-based training is a foundation, and the contract and the employer's Level III decide how the personnel requirements are met.

Engines and propulsion. Williams International builds small gas turbine engines in Ogden, and Northrop Grumman operates large rocket motor facilities in Box Elder County northwest of Ogden. Rotating parts, cases and bonded assemblies use ultrasonic, radiographic, penetrant and magnetic particle methods to demanding customer specifications.

Aerospace and composite suppliers. Northern Utah's machining, composite layup and fabrication shops supply primes in aerospace and defence. These shops often need to show customers a written practice and complete training and examination records before a purchase order is awarded.

Refining, pipelines and process plants. South along the Wasatch Front, refineries and pipeline systems around Salt Lake City use the pressure-equipment methods and codes more familiar in oil and gas, and technicians from Ogden commute to them. See also NDT training in Salt Lake City.

Construction and heavy industry. Structural steel, bridges, mining equipment and fabricated products across Weber and Davis Counties rely on AWS D1.1 visual and magnetic particle inspection.

For earnings information on Ogden-area work, see our NDT salary guide, which cites public sources. Technicians who can document their work to aerospace standards tend to be valued by more than one sector.

NDT schools and classes near Ogden: what to compare

People who search for NDT schools or classes in Ogden find a mix of colleges, private training companies and employer in-house programmes. Some run scheduled classroom courses with a fixed location. Others offer self-paced theory online and leave the practical examination to be done where the technician works. The right choice depends on whether you already have an employer, how much time you can set aside, and how your future employer certifies.

Ask any provider the questions that matter. Who certifies you at the end: the school or an employer under a written practice? Will your prospective employer accept the hours? Who writes and grades the practical examination, and is that person a Level III? In aerospace and defence especially, ask whether the training will line up with the customer flow-down documents your employer works under, since those sometimes demand more than a general course delivers.

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Ogden. If you already have a sponsoring employer, we provide online theory with Level III Q&A and the practical examination at their site. If you are still looking for one, start with the near-me guide and the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker.

Online NDT training in Utah

Technicians in Utah can complete the theory for Level I and II courses online and self-paced on the Atlantis portal, with Level III Q&A on the material. Access opens the moment you enrol, so someone working a day shift at a depot supplier or a manufacturing plant in Ogden can study on their own time. Hands-on training and the practical examination take place in person at the employer's facility, and the employer signs the certification. See online NDT training and the Utah training page.

Online theory covers the classroom portion only. In Ogden, the Level III is available to answer questions while you study, and the portal opens the moment you enrol. In Ogden, courses run year-round, so there is no fixed start date to wait for. Your employer's written practice still decides how many classroom hours count, which is why it helps to ask your Ogden employer before you enrol.

Training a crew at your Ogden facility

An Ogden aerospace or defence supplier that needs several technicians qualified can run the full programme on its own schedule: self-paced theory online, then specific and practical examinations at your facility on your own part families and procedures. Because the specific examination should reflect the procedures your customers have approved, an onsite format means technicians are tested on the work they will actually perform.

Suppliers preparing for customer audits can also have the written practice and records reviewed. See written practice development and corporate NDT training, or ask about training an Ogden crew.

For Ogden candidates the practical examination is hands-on with real equipment and specimens and is never conducted remotely. In Ogden, if you want help writing the Level III side of the programme, see outsourced Level III consulting.

Radiography licensing in Utah

Utah is an NRC Agreement State. The Utah Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control regulates radioactive materials in the state, which includes the sealed sources industrial radiographers use, and it also registers X-ray machines. A radiography employer needs the appropriate licence or registration, and radiographers must meet the training and supervision requirements set out in it and in the state rules. A method course in RT does not provide that authorisation and does not license anyone. Ogden employers normally need both radiation safety authorisation and SNT-TC-1A certification covering technique and interpretation. Confirm current requirements with the Utah Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control before planning radiography work or training.

Practise before your practical exam

The Practical NDT browser simulator lets a Ogden technician rehearse set-ups, scanning coverage and interpretation in virtual workplaces between hands-on sessions, and the NDT practice tests cover the general and method theory. They are rehearsal tools. They do not replace hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens under your Ogden employer's written practice.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Ogden

How do I get NDT certified in Ogden?

Join or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the training and experience it requires, pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and the employer certifies you.

Is there aerospace NDT work in Ogden?

Yes. Hill Air Force Base and the supplier base around it create demand. Postings change, so check employer career pages, and ask suppliers what they require from new technicians.

Will Atlantis training qualify me to work on military aircraft?

A course alone does not. Contractors apply their own written practices and the requirements of the contract. SNT-TC-1A-based training is a foundation, and the employer's Level III decides how requirements are met.

Can I take NDT classes online in Utah?

The theory can be done online at your own pace. Practical work is hands-on with your employer, and the simulator is a rehearsal tool.

Which NDT method should I learn first in northern Utah?

Visual, penetrant and magnetic particle testing are common starting points, followed by ultrasonic. Aerospace suppliers also use radiography and eddy current, so many technicians add methods over time.

How long does Level 2 training take?

The employer's written practice sets the hours. The training-requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours, and experience usually takes the longest.

Can I get Level III training in Ogden?

Yes, preparation is online and self-paced with Level III Q&A. See ASNT Level III training.

Does a course make me certified?

No. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies, so a course provides training and preparation. ASNT central certification is a route not tied to one employer.

Where do I see the published fees?

The published US fees are in the table on this page, and Register and Buy Now opens the course on the Atlantis portal.

Are there other training pages near Ogden?

Yes. Nearby markets with their own guides include Salt Lake City, Idaho Falls, Denver, Billings, and the Utah training page covers the state as a whole.
